The edge: one draft plan, served live, with its notes beside it loden

A static site generated from one repo at one commit: its plans/, their as-built files, and a SCIP index, rendered as HTML with microdata and rel links. A person opens it in a browser and an agent fetches it, and both read the same pages. A small dev server serves it. The data is mock-control at 90c65b9, whose only plan is pumice.

This plan is also the brief. Whoever builds it records what changed in <this plan>.as-built.md, and that file answers this plan's guesses.

Decision: A static site generator plus a dev server, not a running API

Because (Jeff): git is immutable, so the site for a commit is a pure function of the commit and its index. Nothing goes stale; a page is only ever old.

Decision: The HTML is the API

Because (Jeff): the human and the agent should work from exactly the same substrate. Structure is carried by rel links and microdata, not by a separate JSON shape.

Decision: Read-only

Because (Jeff): truth stays in git and markdown. The site is a projection of it, never a place to write.

Decision: Every page says which repo and commit it was generated from

Because (Claude, agreed by Jeff): "code at HEAD" becomes "code at this commit," so a reader can always tell what they're looking at.

Decision: Each anchor is shown at the plan's base and at the generated commit

where mock-control: plans/2026-10-29-pumice.md › Selectors use the library's prefix, `mock-panel`

quote - quote: `selector: 'app-mock-panel',`

in mock-control, which this site doesn't read

Because (measured, mock-control at 90c65b9): anchors point at the base, and the plan's own work moves them. Pumice's selector quote matches at its base da023f1 and not at 90c65b9, because pumice renamed it; the README heading moved for the same reason. Showing only the later commit would make the plan's own work look like drift. v0 shows both, side by side, and doesn't judge the difference.

Decision: SCIP anchors resolve through the index; other anchors by their quote

Because (Claude, agreed by Jeff): the spike showed defn_enclosing_ranges gives a symbol's line range, so its code is a lookup plus git show. Pumice's other anchors are a markdown heading path and a JSON key path; for those, finding the quote in the named file is enough to show the code. When it isn't found, the page says so plainly: "quote not found at <commit>."

Decision: Quote search looks only in the anchor's file

Because (measured): searching the whole repo for pumice's quotes matches the plan itself, which quotes them.

Decision: where (new) anchors are shown, not resolved

Because (Claude, not asked): they have no quote by design. Resolving them means finding where the work landed, which is the drift question, and v0 declines drift.

Decision: Cross-repo anchors are shown as text

Because (Claude, not asked): v0 reads one repo. Lanyard's anchors into pumice are the first case, and they wait.

Decision: Reverse pages, one per anchored symbol or file, listing the plans there

Because (Claude's proposal, unanswered, so its fallback): the first brick of level 3, archaeology, and it makes the link graph go both ways from the start. With one plan each page lists one plan.

Decision: The first rels, and a profile document that defines them

Because (Claude, not asked): v0 can't avoid starting the vocabulary. Registered rels where they fit (profile, item, collection, up); ours are as-built, anchored-at (entry to anchor page), and anchored-by (anchor page to entry). The profile document is one page in the site, and each rel's definition says what question it answers.

Decision: TypeScript, indexing with scip-typescript at the generated commit

Because (Jeff and Claude, aide's CLAUDE.md): start where SCIP indexing is strong. The spike indexed mock-control in about half a second, so indexing each commit it needs (the generated one, and each plan's base) is cheap. Libraries and layout are the builder's call, recorded in the as-built.

Decision: The generated site isn't committed

Because (Jeff and Claude): it's reproducible from the commit, and generated output in git would bury the plans in diff noise. Output goes to a gitignored directory.

Decline: A separate client app

Because (Jeff and Claude): a second representation would let the person and the agent see different things. A client, Angular or otherwise, can come later as one more projection of the same pages.

Decline: A separate brief beside the plan

Because (Claude, agreed by Jeff): two copies of what to build can disagree. Lanyard designed the plan plus as-built for exactly this handoff, and v0 is its first test.

Decline: Drift, guesses and triangulation, the heat map, the LSP adapter, the Angular language service, and cross-company queries

Because (Jeff and Claude): each was raised, and none is needed to walk one plan. They're recorded so nobody adds them helpfully.

Guess: The plan is enough of a brief

Disproved if: the builder has to ask for something this plan doesn't say, or the as-built records a gap that a brief would have filled.

Guess: Quote search is enough for anchors that aren't SCIP symbols

Disproved if: a quote matches more than once in its file at the base, or a reader can't tell from the page which lines the anchor meant.
